These writ petitions arise from and out of the land acquisition proceedings initiated under the National Highways Act, 1956, wherein the lands of the petitioners had been acquired for building (widening/two-laning with paved shoulders etc.,) maintenance, management and operation of National Highways No.210 and 67 for the stretch of land in Trichy  Karaikudi Section from Km.10/000 to Km.94/000 of NH No.210 including Trichy Bypass from Km.109/558 to Km.135/
930 in NH No.67 in Trichirappalli District in the State of Tamil Nadu.
2. It appears that the lands have been acquired and awards had been passed in respect of the said acquisition.

Given below is the chart for easy reference:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.(MD) No.991 of 2020 etc., batch Sl.
Writ Name of the Total Award Date No.
Petition Petitioner Survey No. Compensation (MD) No.
The above chart would give details of the respective writ petitions, date of passing of the award and the proceedings initiated thereon.

3. The petitioners are aggrieved by the fact that they have not been awarded solatium and interest,
which they are entitled to as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Union of India and another Vs. Tarsem Singh & Ors. reported in (2019) 9 SCC 304, in which the Hon'ble Supreme Court, which was considering similar acquisition under the National Highways Act, where solatium and interest had not been granted, ultimately observed as follows:

entities.text: Union of India and another Vs. Tarsem Singh & Ors. reported in (2019) 9 SCC 304
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We therefore declare that the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act relating to solatium and interest contained in Section 23(1A) and (2) and interest payable in terms of Section 28 proviso will apply to acquisitions made under the National Highways Act.
Consequently, the provision of Section 3J is, to this extent, violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India and, therefore, declared to be unconstitutional.

Mr.D.Ghandiraj, learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the first respondent and the learned counsel appearing for respondents 2 and 3 would submit that some of the petitioners have not exhausted the remedy available to them under the National Highways Act and have approached this Court with a great delay.
The procedure under the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) contemplates a time bound disposal of the claims and the appeals thereon.
5. The main defence raised by the respondents is with reference to the delay.

This issue has been considered by a Division Bench of this Court in the case of The Project Director, Project Implementation Unit, NHAI, Vs. K.Periyasamy and others reported in 2018 SCC OnLine Mad 13839 wherein the question that required the attention of the Division Bench was whether the provisions of the Limitation Act, 1963, particularly Article 137 would apply to an application seeking A r b i t r a t i o n u n d e r S e c t i o n 3 - G ( 5 ) o f t h e N a t i o n a l H i g h w a y s A c t , 1 9 5 6 .
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.(MD) No.991 of 2020 etc., batch 6.

entities.text: Project Director, Project Implementation Unit, NHAI, Vs. K.Periyasamy and others reported in 2018 SCC OnLine Mad 13839
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Bench, after discussing the scheme of the Act particularly with reference to Section 3-G of the National Highways Act and Sections 21 and 43 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and the various judgments in relation to the statutory arbitrations, had ultimately held that the provisions of the Limitation Act more particularly Article 137 would not apply to a reference to Section 3-G of the Act.
The provision of the Limitation Act would not apply to statutory arbitrations more particularly arbitration under Section 3-G(5) of the Act.
Therefore, the petitions before this Court cannot be non-suited on the ground of limitation.

7. All the parties have now consented to this Court for passing the following order:
(i) It is informed that with reference to the writ petitions in W.P.(MD) Nos.991 and 1033 of 2020 (Sl.Nos.1 and 8 in the chart), the petitioners are dead and their legal representatives have not come forward to contact the counsel for bringing them on records.

Therefore, W.P.(MD) Nos.991 and 1033 of 2020 are dismissed as abated;
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.(MD) No.991 of 2020 etc., batch

(ii) As regards W.P.(MD) Nos.1024, 1068, 1075 and 2942 of 2020 (Sl.Nos.6, 11, 13 and 14 in the chart), the learned counsel for the petitioners submits that claim petitions filed before the respective District Collectors had been disposed of and the parties have filed application under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act, before the concerned Principal District Judge and the matter is now pending before the District Court; and (iii) As regards the petitioners in W.P.(MD) Nos.1014, 1016, 1018, 1019, 1025, 1036, 1038 and 1073 of 2020 (Sl.Nos.2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 and 12), some of them have filed application, while the others are yet to file application.

However, taking into account the fact that the petitioners are entitled to solatium and interest by virtue of the judgment referred above and since the same has not been granted to them, the petitioners shall file claim petition before the respective District Collectors within a period of two weeks from the date of S.Palraj vs Authorized Officer/Special District ... on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15366672/
4 receipt of a copy of this order.
Thereafter, the respective District Collectors shall pass orders.
The entire process shall be completed within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
